university: University of Arkansas at Little Rock

documents.unit: Office of the Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost
documents.title: Resources for Faculty on Student Use of AI
documents.stance_why: The page tells faculty to 'explicitly state your policies on AI tools' and to give 'specific examples of acceptable and unacceptable uses', so the rule is set by each instructor in the syllabus; the page itself sets no ban or permission, hence delegates.
documents.summary: Provost guidance for faculty on stating AI expectations, recognizing signs of AI use, using detectors only as one input, and reporting suspected misuse through integrity procedures. It leaves the actual AI rule to each instructor.

units.why: The sentence directs instructors to 'explicitly state your policies on AI tools'; it binds instructors at course start, so P09 (statement required) rather than P04, because it requires a statement rather than saying who decides.
units.anchor: explicitly state your policies on AI tools such as chatbots, language models, and writing assistants
units.frag_start: At the beginning of each course

units.why: 'Include these guidelines in your syllabus' tells instructors where the AI policy goes, so P09 (AI statement in syllabus), addressed to instructors at course start.
units.anchor: Include these guidelines in your syllabus
units.policy: Instructors include their AI guidelines in the syllabus.

units.why: 'discuss them in class to emphasize their importance' asks instructors to talk through the rules beyond listing them, which is P66 rather than P09.
units.anchor: discuss them in class to emphasize their importance
units.policy: Instructors discuss their AI guidelines in class to emphasize their importance.

units.why: 'providing specific examples of acceptable and unacceptable uses' advises concrete examples so students avoid 'unintentional violations'; this is explaining rules beyond the bare statement (P66).
units.anchor: specific examples of acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI
units.policy: Instructors provide specific examples of acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI to help students avoid unintentional violations of academic integrity.

units.why: The page says 'Detecting the use of AI in student work can be challenging', acknowledging limits on verification, so P82 (informs).
units.anchor: Detecting the use of AI in student work can be challenging
units.policy: Detecting the use of AI in student work can be challenging.

units.why: The list of signs ('unusual consistency in tone or style', 'overly generic or repetitive phrases') names kinds of evidence to weigh when judging AI misuse, which is P69; it is not P40 because no tool is involved.
units.anchor: Look for unusual consistency in tone or style
units.fit_note: Lists indicators of AI use (generic phrasing, lack of analysis, too-advanced work) rather than a standard of proof.

units.why: 'Platforms like Turnitin now offer AI-detection features' presents detectors as available tools to identify AI content, so P40 (detectors used to identify misuse).
units.anchor: Platforms like Turnitin now offer AI-detection features that can flag sections of text

units.why: Grammarly is named as a plagiarism and AI-detection tool, a listed means of identifying misuse, so P40.
units.anchor: Grammarly and other writing assistants with plagiarism detection capabilities may also indicate potential AI use

units.why: 'use these tools as part of a broader assessment rather than relying on them exclusively' says detector output is supporting evidence only, matching the broadened P69 (not P39, which says detectors are unreliable or not used).
units.anchor: use these tools as part of a broader assessment rather than relying on them exclusively
units.frag_end: work to make a well-informed decision.
units.policy: Detection tools are used as part of a broader assessment, not relied on exclusively, and combined with the instructor's judgment and knowledge of students' work.

units.why: 'Begin by discussing your concerns with the student' tells instructors to talk with the student before reporting, i.e. P57.
units.anchor: Begin by discussing your concerns with the student
units.policy: Instructors begin by discussing their concerns with the student when they suspect improper AI use.

units.why: 'giving them an opportunity to explain their process and intentions' gives the accused student a chance to respond, so P64 (right to respond).
units.anchor: giving them an opportunity to explain their process and intentions
units.policy: Students suspected of improper AI use are given an opportunity to explain their process and intentions.

units.why: 'follow your institution's procedures for addressing academic integrity violations' sends suspected AI misuse into the formal procedure, so P81 (procedural steps) over P36 because it is about process rather than classifying misuse.
units.anchor: follow your institution’s procedures for addressing academic integrity violations
units.frag_start: If you suspect a student has
units.policy: Instructors who suspect improper AI use follow the institution's procedures for addressing academic integrity violations.

units.why: 'report the incident to the appropriate academic integrity office or committee, providing documentation' is a reporting step with required documentation, so P81.
units.anchor: report the incident to the appropriate academic integrity office or committee
units.policy: If necessary, instructors report the incident to the appropriate academic integrity office or committee, providing documentation of their findings and any relevant evidence from detection tools.

units.why: 'clearly explain how the student’s use of AI violated your course policies' is a content requirement of the report and ties the case to the instructor's own stated policy, so P81.
units.anchor: clearly explain how the student’s use of AI violated your course policies
units.policy: In the report, instructors clearly explain how the student's use of AI violated their course policies.

units.why: 'Maintaining transparency and fairness throughout this process is essential' states a fairness principle for AI-misuse cases, closest to P64 (fairness and transparency in AI-related integrity cases).
units.anchor: Maintaining transparency and fairness throughout this process is essential
units.frag_end: misusing AI in their academic work.
units.policy: Maintaining transparency and fairness throughout the process of addressing AI misuse is essential to uphold academic standards.
units.fit_note: States a general fairness and transparency principle rather than a student right to respond.

units.why: The closing line frames the resources as helping 'students and instructors ... leverage these technologies responsibly and effectively', a statement of purpose for the guidance, so P56.
units.anchor: ensuring that both students and instructors can leverage these technologies responsibly and effectively
units.policy: The resources are intended to support faculty in navigating AI and LLMs in academia so that students and instructors can leverage these technologies responsibly and effectively.
units.fit_note: Purpose statement for a resource page, not a full institution-wide framework.

documents.unit: Office of the Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost
documents.title: Purpose Statement on Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: The statement sets out to 'foster a culture of technological proficiency' and to 'Encourage the development of AI literacy and skills' while 'safeguarding against its risks'; it welcomes responsible AI use but sets no student-level rules, so encourage rather than delegates.
documents.summary: A university-wide principles statement presenting AI as an opportunity for teaching, research and administration, naming risks (privacy, bias, misuse), and listing goals including AI literacy. It sets no rules for coursework.

units.why: 'establish a comprehensive framework for the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence' states the scope and purpose for faculty, staff and students, so P56.
units.anchor: establish a comprehensive framework for the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence
units.frag_start: The purpose of this information is to
units.frag_end: at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock.
units.policy: The purpose is to establish a comprehensive framework for the responsible use of AI among faculty, staff, and students.

units.why: 'enhance learning experiences through personalized education, streamline administrative tasks, and drive innovative research' lists benefits of AI, so P87 rather than a rule.
units.anchor: It can enhance learning experiences through personalized education
units.frag_start: AI and machine learning (ML) has the potential
units.policy: AI and ML can enhance learning experiences through personalized education, streamline administrative tasks, and drive innovative research across disciplines.

units.why: 'preparing our community for future careers and societal contributions' gives career readiness as the reason for integrating AI, which is P44.
units.anchor: preparing our community for future careers and societal contributions
units.policy: By integrating AI responsibly, the university aims to foster a culture of technological proficiency, creativity, and critical thinking, preparing the community for future careers and societal contributions.

units.why: 'data privacy, algorithmic bias, and the potential for misuse require careful consideration' names ethical risks, so P53; privacy is also mentioned but bias is the main ethical concern named.
units.anchor: Issues such as data privacy, algorithmic bias, and the potential for misuse require careful consideration
units.policy: Issues such as data privacy, algorithmic bias, and the potential for misuse require careful consideration and proactive management.
units.fit_note: Also names data privacy and misuse, not only bias, harms and environmental cost.

units.why: 'ensure that AI applications align with our core values of equity, transparency, and accountability' sets principles for AI applications, so P56.
units.anchor: ensure that AI applications align with our core values of equity, transparency, and accountability
units.policy: AI applications must align with the university's core values of equity, transparency, and accountability.

units.why: 'Promote the ethical and effective use of AI in teaching, research, and administration' is a stated goal covering all three domains, so P56.
units.anchor: Promote the ethical and effective use of AI in teaching, research, and administration
units.policy: The information is designed to promote the ethical and effective use of AI in teaching, research, and administration.

units.why: 'Encourage the development of AI literacy and skills among all members' commits the university to AI literacy, matching P70.
units.anchor: Encourage the development of AI literacy and skills among all members of our university community
units.policy: The information is designed to encourage the development of AI literacy and skills among all members of the university community.
units.fit_note: Goal to encourage AI literacy; no specific training or module is named.

units.why: 'Ensure that AI technologies are deployed in a manner that upholds our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion' is an equity goal for AI deployment; no existing type covers deployment under DEI commitments (P51 is cost and access, P53 is harms).
units.anchor: deployed in a manner that upholds our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion
units.policy: AI technologies are deployed in a manner that upholds the university's commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion.
units.uncovered_note: AI deployment must uphold the institution's diversity, equity and inclusion commitments.

units.why: 'Foster interdisciplinary collaboration in AI research and application' is a goal about collaboration across disciplines; it is not peer or community engagement (P88) nor a research-use rule (P62).
units.anchor: Foster interdisciplinary collaboration in AI research and application
units.policy: The information is designed to foster interdisciplinary collaboration in AI research and application.
units.uncovered_note: Goal of fostering interdisciplinary collaboration in AI research and application inside the university.

documents.unit: Office of the Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost
documents.title: Resources for Students on Use of AI
documents.stance_why: The page tells students to 'review your syllabus carefully for any specific guidelines your instructors have set', so AI rules are set by individual instructors and the page sets none itself.
documents.summary: A short student resource page pointing to an ethics course, plagiarism and AI-detection tools, citation guidance and the Academic Offenses policy, and telling students to check each syllabus and ask instructors when unsure.

units.why: 'Review your syllabus carefully for any specific guidelines' makes students responsible for finding the course's AI rules, which is P78 rather than P10 (ask when unsure).
units.anchor: Review your syllabus carefully for any specific guidelines your instructors have set regarding AI use
units.policy: Students review their syllabus carefully for any specific guidelines their instructors have set regarding AI use.

units.why: 'guidelines your instructors have set regarding AI use ... restrictions on AI assistance or requirements for disclosing' shows that individual instructors set AI rules, so P04.
units.anchor: This could include restrictions on AI assistance or requirements for disclosing AI contributions
units.policy: Instructors set course-specific guidelines on AI use, which may include restrictions on AI assistance or requirements for disclosing AI contributions.

units.why: 'If you are unsure ... reach out to your professor for clarification and guidance' is the ask-first rule, P10.
units.anchor: reach out to your professor for clarification and guidance
units.frag_start: If you’re unsure about how to use
units.policy: Students who are unsure how to use AI tools in a course reach out to their professor for clarification and guidance.

units.why: Free ethics course listed under 'Online Learning Modules' is an AI-ethics training resource for students, P70.
units.anchor: Kaggle: Intro to Ethics Free Online Course with Certificate of Completion
units.policy: The university lists the Kaggle Intro to Ethics free online course with certificate of completion as a learning module on ethical AI use.
units.fit_note: A pointer to an external ethics course, not a mandate or institutional module.

units.why: Grammarly is offered to students for 'plagiarism checking and alerts for potential AI-generated content, helping students ensure their work is original', a student self-check tool that no existing type covers (P40 is staff-side identification of misuse).
units.anchor: alerts for potential AI-generated content, helping students ensure their work is original
units.policy: Grammarly offers plagiarism checking and alerts for potential AI-generated content, helping students ensure their work is original.
units.uncovered_note: Students are pointed to a tool that checks their own work for plagiarism and AI-generated content.

units.why: Pointing students to 'Purdue Information on Citing AI' signals that AI use should be cited and gives citation guidance, P24 loosely.
units.anchor: Purdue Information on Citing AI
units.fit_note: Only a link to external citation guidance; no stated requirement to cite.

documents.title: LR 501.13 Academic Offenses (academic integrity and grievance)
documents.stance_why: The policy lists 'Using unauthorized notes or materials (including any form of generative AI)' as cheating and treats AI content 'without proper acknowledgement' as plagiarism, so generative AI is barred unless authorized or acknowledged; that is restrict.
documents.summary: The Faculty Senate academic offenses policy covers all academic dishonesty; it names unauthorized generative AI as cheating and unacknowledged generative AI as plagiarism, then sets the report, conference, grade-penalty, hearing and appeal procedure. Only two sentences mention AI, but the procedure applies to AI cases.

units.why: Listing 'Using unauthorized notes or materials (including any form of generative AI)' under cheating makes unauthorized generative AI misconduct, P36 over P22 because it is not limited to exams.
units.anchor: Using unauthorized notes or materials (including any form of generative AI)

units.why: The sentence says using 'products produced by any form of Generative AI without proper acknowledgement' is plagiarism: it sets an acknowledgement duty (P24) and classes failure as plagiarism. I chose P24 because a reader looking for disclosure rules expects it there.
units.anchor: using ideas, words, or products produced by any form of Generative AI without proper acknowledgement
units.frag_end: published work as new without disclosure (self-plagiarism).
units.policy: Using ideas, words, or products produced by any form of Generative AI without proper acknowledgement is plagiarism.
units.fit_note: Also classifies unacknowledged generative AI use as plagiarism (an academic offense).

units.why: 'Academic offenses are not permitted under any circumstances and are a violation of student conduct standards' is the general rule under which the AI items fall, P36.
units.anchor: Academic offenses are not permitted under any circumstances
units.fit_note: General academic-offense rule; AI is covered only through the cheating and plagiarism definitions.

units.why: 'Students must not pursue an unfair advantage over classmates through deception or dishonesty' grounds the rule in fairness, P95.
units.anchor: Students must not pursue an unfair advantage over classmates through deception or dishonesty

units.why: Instructors are told they are responsible for 'Taking reasonable steps to prevent academic dishonesty', a preventive duty; P99 is the nearest, though it names no specific measures.
units.anchor: Taking reasonable steps to prevent academic dishonesty
units.fit_note: General duty to prevent dishonesty without naming any measures.

units.why: 'Reporting all suspected academic offenses to the Office of the Dean of Students' is a required reporting step, P81.
units.anchor: Reporting all suspected academic offenses to the Office of the Dean of Students
units.frag_end: Office of the Dean of Students

units.why: Students are responsible for 'Fully acknowledging all borrowed ideas and materials', the acknowledgement duty that governs AI-generated material too, P24.
units.anchor: Fully acknowledging all borrowed ideas and materials

units.why: 'A finding that work resulted from dishonest action may affect the grading of the specific assignment and/or the overall final grade' states possible grade consequences, P37.
units.anchor: may affect the grading of the specific assignment and/or the overall final grade
units.policy: A finding that work resulted from dishonest action may affect the grading of the specific assignment and/or the overall final grade in the course, and disciplinary action may be imposed by the Office of the Dean of Students or AOGAC.
units.fit_note: Lists possible consequences without fixing a penalty for each offense.

units.why: 'Grade Penalties May Include F in the course / F on the assignment or exam' lists concrete penalties, P37.
units.anchor: F in the course
units.policy: Grade penalties may include F in the course, F on the assignment or exam, grade adjustment, or no credit for material presented.

units.why: 'Within five class days of identifying the suspected offense, the instructor must' complete the form is a deadline-bound reporting step, P81.
units.anchor: Within five class days of identifying the suspected offense, the instructor must
units.frag_start: Within five class days of identifying
units.policy: Within five class days of identifying a suspected offense, the instructor must complete the Allegation of Academic Offense Form, send it to the student, retain a copy, and send copies to the department chair and the Office of the Dean of Students.

units.why: The instructor notice 'must specify the allegation' and 'Include supporting evidence', setting an evidence requirement for the notice, P69.
units.anchor: Include supporting evidence
units.policy: The instructor's notice must specify the allegation and include supporting evidence.
units.fit_note: Requires supporting evidence in the notice but sets no standard of what counts.

units.why: The conference exists to 'Allow the student to present an explanation or response', giving the accused a right to respond, P64.
units.anchor: Allow the student to present an explanation or response
units.policy: The student-instructor conference exists to ensure the student understands the allegation and evidence and to allow the student to present an explanation or response.

units.why: 'A grade penalty may be imposed only by the instructor, and only after required procedural steps are completed' makes the penalty depend on process, P81.
units.anchor: A grade penalty may be imposed only by the instructor
units.frag_start: A grade penalty may be imposed only

units.why: 'Student may continue attending class during appeal' is part of the appeal rights that let a student contest an allegation, P64.
units.anchor: Student may continue attending class during appeal
units.policy: Students may appeal an academic offense finding and may continue attending class during the appeal.
units.fit_note: Covers appeal rights for any academic-offense allegation, not AI specifically.

units.why: Instructors 'should consider: Severity, Context, Comparable cases, Student circumstances' sets factors for choosing a penalty, P37 loosely.
units.anchor: Instructors should consider
units.policy: Instructors should consider severity, context, comparable cases, and student circumstances when imposing a grade penalty.
units.fit_note: Gives factors for choosing a penalty rather than stating a specific penalty.

documents.title: LR 404.8 Course Syllabus
documents.stance_why: The policy requires each syllabus to contain 'The instructor’s statement on the permissibility of student use of generative AI', handing the permit-or-ban decision to the instructor, so delegates.
documents.summary: The syllabus policy lists required elements of every course syllabus. One element is the instructor's statement on whether students may use generative AI for assignments and course activities.

units.why: The syllabus must contain 'The instructor’s statement on the permissibility of student use of generative AI'; this requires an AI statement in every syllabus (P09) and leaves the decision to the instructor (P04). I chose P09 because the sentence is a required element, not a statement of who decides.
units.anchor: statement on the permissibility of student use of generative AI
units.frag_start: The instructor’s statement on the permissibility
units.policy: The syllabus must contain the instructor's statement on the permissibility of student use of generative AI (such as large language models) for completion of assignments and other course activities.

notes: Coder A. No school, computing or course documents were in scope. LR 501.13 is a general academic-offense procedure; only the AI-relevant lines plus core process steps that apply to AI cases are coded.
